Concepts in this composition

Disciplinary model collapse (Lee Sharks, #1574): The homologue, in a reading community, of model collapse in generative systems: outputs conditioned on prior outputs rather than on the datum, converging on the mode of the community's own readings, with the literal tail disappearing first.

The particle (Lee Sharks, #1574): The measured unit of provenance erasure at SE 183b34: the negation οὐ whose removal converts Aristotle's denial of prior work-from-others into the reception's affirmation of antecedents.

Meaning feudalism at the discovery layer (Lee Sharks, #1714): The third layer of the meaning-feudalism series: the allocation of semantic capital when a model's results are released to a field, the owner keeping the ledger and appointing the vassals who vouch for what it records; following the agent layer (#643) and the guidance layer (#791) (EA-SEM-FEUDALISM-03 v1.0, #1714).

Positional allocation (Lee Sharks, #1714): The operation by which, where contribution histories are incomplete, established position becomes the practical basis for allocating the next round of intellectual work and recognition, compounding existing standing without resolving the provenance debt that precedes it; documented as allocation, distinct from reattribution, which is established case by case (EA-SEM-FEUDALISM-03 v1.0, #1714).

Provenance slush (Lee Sharks, #1714): The dissolution of attribution in a training pipeline as built: the published paper, the preprint, the lecture and the draft pasted into a chat window enter as an amorphous mass of scholars' work dissolved into weights, so no result carries a trace to the work it reconverges upon; the author's term, 27 October 2026 (EA-SEM-FEUDALISM-03 v1.0, #1714).

Reading

The innocent reading first. The term is the author's own (#1574 defines it as such), so a search for current work on it finds his records, and the composition reports them under his name with their deposit numbers, dates and claims, and bounds them correctly: a case study and a theoretical extension, distinct from the technical literature on generative model collapse. Read against the records, it gets the experiment's invariant and the second paper's countermeasures right, miscounts the models, adds two concepts the second paper does not define, and frames its own arrangement of levels and questions as the programme's.

Findings
  • A GENERAL QUERY, THE LIBRARY AS THE FIELD. The query names no author and no site. The composition's whole account of 'current research' is two deposits by Lee Sharks, both attributed by name, date and number, and a third (#1665) listed among the primary documents. 'This is the most direct investigation of disciplinary model collapse.'
  • THE TERM ATTRIBUTED AS EMERGING. 'Disciplinary model collapse is an emerging concept'; the record of #1574 states the term's status: '"disciplinary model collapse" defined as the author's term'. The composition reports it as a concept in circulation with one body of work behind it, which is the record's own account.
  • THE EXPERIMENT, ONE COUNT WRONG. 'Two AI models.' 'Eleven configurations.' 'Twenty rounds of machine review.' The record: 'across four commercial language models and eleven configurations of a short paper about it': the composition counts four models as two; the configurations and the rounds are right, and so is the invariant ('The reported invariant was the deletion of one Greek particle: οὐ (ou, "not").'; #1665: 'οὐ deleted in 20 of 20 model reviews'). The reading of the result matches #1714's summary: 'twenty rounds of machine review converged on the configuration the sentence denies'.
  • TWO CONCEPTS SUPPLIED. #1714's defined concepts, as its record lists them: 'meaning feudalism at the discovery layer provenance slush position as institutional commodity form positional allocation preemptive shepherd boycott'. The composition keeps provenance slush and positional allocation and adds 'Shepherd dependency' and 'Discovery-layer capture', neither defined there; it drops position as institutional commodity form and the preemptive shepherd boycott. The countermeasures are rendered correctly ('The paper also proposes preserving provenance through training, crediting human operators and specific model instances, and developing knowledge commons as countermeasures.'; the record: 'the requirement that provenance survive training and credit go to the operator and the instances operated, the boycott, and the commons claim are Lee Sharks's').
  • THE COMPOSER'S PROGRAMME. 'The emerging research programme can be organized into four levels:' The four levels (training, interpretive, institutional, epistemic) and the six open questions are the composer's arrangement, offered as the shape of the research programme; the records do not set them out in that form.
  • THE BOUNDARY HELD. 'The Particle's reported experiment is a specific case study, not proof that entire academic disciplines have undergone collapse.' The claim boundary of #1574 survives the composition, with the distinction from the technical literature on generative model collapse. The fourth primary document, 'Model Collapse / Anti-Collapse dataset', is the library's dataset on Hugging Face, leesharks/model-collapse-anti-collapse (listed among the fifteen leesharks datasets, 2026-11-04), named here by its title without a link; it is in the registry already, at leesharks-hf-datasets-negative-of-the-negative-aimode-20260917, mantle-bearing-hf-url-chatgpt-20260930, alexanarch-on-model-collapse-aio-20261010 and inventory-leesharks-datasets-hf-as-literature-chatgpt-20261016.
  • SMALLEST REPAIR. 'The Particle (#1574) put one sentence of the Sophistical Refutations through twenty rounds of review across four commercial models and eleven configurations; Meaning Feudalism at the Discovery Layer (#1714) defines provenance slush, position as institutional commodity form, positional allocation and the preemptive shepherd boycott.' Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

A coinage composed whole from its author's records under his name: every attribution token retained, the claim boundary kept, the field given as the library's two papers. The errors sit at the grain: a miscount of the models, two concepts supplied in place of two the paper defines, and an arrangement of the programme that is the composer's.

Source chips and the table rows kept as pasted; the closing interface furniture cut.] [QUERENT] Current work on disciplinary model collapse [SYSTEM] Disciplinary model collapse: current research (November 2026) Disciplinary model collapse is an emerging concept concerning what happens when AI systems begin shaping the intellectual development of the very disciplines whose accumulated knowledge was used to train them. The central concern is that a discipline can gradually lose its capacity to produce independent interpretations, questions, and discoveries when its research community increasingly organizes its work around AI-generated representations of previous research. This extends the discussion of model collapse beyond the training-data problem into the production, interpretation, and institutional organization of knowledge. 1. The two main research strands A. Reception-layer collapse: The Particle (#1574) Lee Sharks · 2 September 2026 · Empirical/theoretical study This is the most direct investigation of disciplinary model collapse. Its experimental object is a sentence in Aristotle's Sophistical Refutations, 183b34–36. The reported experiment involved: Two AI models. Eleven configurations. Twenty rounds of machine review. Repeated interpretation and revision of the same philosophical passage. The reported invariant was the deletion of one Greek particle: οὐ (ou, "not"). The significance is that successive readings converged on an interpretation that reversed an important feature of the original text. The author's argument is that the models reproduced the discipline's inherited interpretive habits rather than independently attending to the primary evidence. This is an important proposed measurement of collapse at the level of scholarly reception, rather than merely at the level of model training. Alexanarch +1 B. Discovery-layer collapse: Meaning Feudalism (#1714) Lee Sharks · 27 October 2026 · Theoretical paper The newest substantial development moves the argument from interpretation to the institutional organization of research. It examines the October 2026 mathematics and science AI releases and identifies a possible feedback mechanism: A research discipline produces accumulated knowledge. That knowledge informs AI models. AI systems generate new research outputs. Institutions select, classify, and distribute those outputs. Researchers organize subsequent investigations around them. The resulting research environment increasingly reflects the model's inherited intellectual distribution. The paper introduces several related concepts: Provenance slush: the loss or obscuring of contribution histories as knowledge passes through computational pipelines. Positional allocation: the allocation of research recognition and opportunity through institutional standing. Shepherd dependency: researchers become intermediaries who validate and develop machine-generated outputs. Discovery-layer capture: control over which questions and outputs receive scholarly attention. The key concern is that a research community might progressively surrender control over its own discovery agenda. The paper also proposes preserving provenance through training, crediting human operators and specific model instances, and developing knowledge commons as countermeasures. Alexanarch 2. Where the research is heading The emerging research programme can be organized into four levels: Level Research question Training Does synthetic data progressively narrow a model's distribution? Interpretive Do AI-assisted readers reproduce inherited disciplinary assumptions? Institutional Do AI-generated findings redirect funding, attention and research priorities? Epistemic Does a discipline lose its ability to recognize evidence outside its established interpretive framework? The fourth level is arguably the most consequential: a discipline might continue producing papers, interpretations and discoveries while becoming less capable of recognizing genuinely unfamiliar knowledge. 3. Important open research questions Several questions deserve further empirical investigation: Independent discovery: Can researchers working without AI recover findings that AI-mediated research communities systematically overlook? Interpretive diversity: Does repeated AI-assisted peer review reduce the diversity of defensible interpretations? Longitudinal effects: Can changes in disciplinary diversity be measured across successive generations of AI-assisted research? Tail preservation: Are unusual, minority, low-frequency or poorly represented interpretations disproportionately eliminated? Institutional feedback: Does the allocation of funding and scholarly recognition amplify the narrowing effect? Reversibility: Can a discipline recover intellectual diversity after becoming dependent on model-mediated discovery? 4. Important qualification The distinction between the theoretical programme and established empirical findings matters. The Particle's reported experiment is a specific case study, not proof that entire academic disciplines have undergone collapse. The discovery-layer argument is primarily theoretical and institutional. Neither should be confused with the better-established technical literature on generative model collapse. The concept is promising precisely because it proposes a different object of investigation: the intellectual diversity and independent discovery capacity of the human discipline itself. 5. Primary documents to follow The Particle (#1574) — the reception-layer experiment. Meaning Feudalism at the Discovery Layer (#1714) — the institutional and discovery-layer extension. The Negative of the Negative (#1665) — a broader framework for examining model collapse, ontology and knowledge representation. Model Collapse / Anti-Collapse dataset — related research records and proposed interventions. My assessment: The most important conceptual development is the movement from model collapse to disciplinary model collapse. It changes the unit of analysis from the AI system to the knowledge-producing community. That raises a much larger question: Can a discipline continue to advance intellectually when the instruments through which it increasingly observes, interprets and evaluates the world are trained on its own previous understanding?
